title: Hello World
description:
Every C journey starts with a first program. Write a program that prints exactly `Hello, World!` followed by a new line.

Input
The program takes no input.

Output
Print `Hello, World!` on one line.
hint: Use `printf` with a string literal. Include the newline in the printed text.
solutionNotes: Include `stdio.h` for `printf`. Print the exact requested text and a newline with `\n`.
constraints: Output must match exactly, including capitalization and punctuation.

title: Print Two Lines
description:
Print the text `Learning C` on the first line and `is fun!` on the second line.

Input
No input.

Output
Two lines exactly as described.
hint: You can print both pieces in one `printf` using `\n`, or use two print calls.
solutionNotes: A newline escape separates the two lines. Keep spelling, punctuation, and capitalization exact.

title: Sum of Two Integers
description:
Read two integers and print their sum.

Input
Two integers separated by a space.

Output
A single integer: their sum.
hint: Read both values with `scanf`, then add the two variables.
solutionNotes: Read both integers with `scanf`, add them, and print the sum followed by a newline.

title: Echo an Integer
description:
Read one integer and print it back as `You entered: N`, where N is the number.

Input
A single integer.

Output
One line: `You entered: ` followed by the integer.
hint: Read one integer into a variable, then print the label and value with `%d`.
solutionNotes: Read one integer into `n`, then use `%d` to insert it after the required label.

title: Difference of Two Numbers
description:
Read two integers `a` and `b` and print `a - b`.

Input
Two integers separated by a space.

Output
One integer: a minus b.
hint: Keep the input order: subtract the second value from the first.
solutionNotes: Read `a` and `b` in order. The requested result is `a - b`, not the reverse.

title: Print a Star Box
description:
Print a box of stars with 3 rows and 5 columns.

Input
No input.

Output
Three lines, each containing `*****`.
hint: Print the same five-star row three times; a short loop can repeat it.
solutionNotes: The loop repeats the same five-star row three times, printing a newline after each row.

title: Greet by Name
description:
Read a single word (a name without spaces) and print `Hello, NAME!`.

Input
One word.

Output
One line: `Hello, ` followed by the name and `!`.
hint: Store the word in a character array, then use `%s` in your greeting.
solutionNotes: The character array stores the input word. `%s` prints it between the fixed greeting text.
constraints: The name has 1 to 40 letters and no spaces.

title: Print a Character Twice
description:
Read one character and print it two times in a row on one line.

Input
One character.

Output
The character repeated twice, e.g. `aa`.
hint: Read one character with `%c` and pass it to two `%c` placeholders.
solutionNotes: The leading space in the `%c` scan format skips whitespace. Two `%c` placeholders print the character twice.
constraints: The character is a letter or digit.

title: Product of Three Numbers
description:
Read three integers and print their product.

Input
Three integers separated by spaces.

Output
One integer: the product.
hint: Read three integers and multiply all three values together.
solutionNotes: Read all three integers and multiply them. The stated bounds keep the product within an `int`.

title: Reverse Two Numbers
description:
Read two integers `a` and `b` and print them in the opposite order, separated by a single space.

Input
Two integers separated by a space.

Output
One line: `b a`.
hint: Read both values, then print the second variable before the first.
solutionNotes: Both inputs are read normally; the output format prints `b` first and `a` second.

title: Average of Three Numbers
description:
Read three integers and print their average with exactly 2 digits after the decimal point.

Input
Three integers separated by spaces.

Output
The average with exactly 2 decimals.
hint: Add the values, divide by `3.0` to keep a fractional result, and format to two decimals.
solutionNotes: Adding the integers gives the numerator. Dividing by `3.0` performs floating-point division, and `%.2f` prints two decimal places.

title: Right Triangle of Stars
description:
Read `n` and print a right triangle of stars with `n` rows. Row `i` has `i` stars.

Input
One integer n.

Output
n lines; line i contains i stars and nothing else.
hint: Use an outer loop for rows and an inner loop that prints as many stars as the row number.
solutionNotes: The outer loop selects each row. The inner loop prints one star per row number, then a newline ends that row.

title: Seconds to Hours Minutes Seconds
description:
Convert a number of seconds into hours, minutes and seconds.

Input
One integer s.

Output
One line: `H hours M minutes S seconds` using the numbers.
hint: Extract hours with division by 3600; use remainders to get the remaining minutes and seconds.
solutionNotes: Integer division by 3600 gives hours. Remainders remove full hours and minutes to get each remaining part.

title: Sum of Digits of a Three-Digit Number
description:
Read a three-digit positive integer and print the sum of its digits.

Input
One integer n.

Output
The sum of the digits.
hint: Use division and remainder: hundreds are `n / 100`, tens are `n / 10 % 10`, and ones are `n % 10`.
solutionNotes: Integer division extracts the hundreds digit; `%` isolates the tens and ones digits. Add the three values.

title: ASCII Code of a Character
description:
Read a single character and print its ASCII code as an integer, then the next character in the ASCII table, on a second line.

Input
One character (a letter or digit, not `z`, `Z` or `9`).

Output
Line 1: the ASCII code. Line 2: the character that follows it.
hint: A `char` can be printed as a number with `%d`; adding one gives the next ASCII character.
solutionNotes: A character is promoted to an integer for `%d`. Adding one produces the next character for `%c`.
constraints: The character is a letter or digit other than z, Z, 9.

title: Print a Simple Receipt
description:
Read the unit price and quantity of an item (both integers) and print a receipt of three lines:
`Price: P`
`Quantity: Q`
`Total: T`
where T is price times quantity.

Input
Two integers: price and quantity.

Output
Three lines as shown.
hint: Read price and quantity, calculate their product, then print each labeled line in the requested order.
solutionNotes: Multiply price by quantity for the total. Print all three lines with their exact labels and order.

title: Echo a Full Line
description:
Read one whole line of text (it may contain spaces) and print it back inside angle brackets, like `<text>`.

Input
One line of text.

Output
The line wrapped in `<` and `>`.
hint: `fgets` reads spaces too. Remove its trailing newline before wrapping the text in angle brackets.
solutionNotes: `fgets` reads spaces and the newline. `strcspn` finds the line ending so it can be removed before printing.
constraints: The line has 1 to 80 characters and ends with a newline.

title: Add Minutes to a Time
description:
Given a time on a 24-hour clock and a number of minutes to add, print the new time. The time wraps around past midnight.

Input
Three integers: hour h, minute m, and minutes to add k.

Output
The new time as `HH:MM` with two digits each.
hint: Convert the time to total minutes, add the offset, wrap with `% 1440`, then split into hours and minutes.
solutionNotes: Represent the time as minutes since midnight, add `k`, and wrap within a day using `% 1440`. Divide and take the remainder to format hours and minutes.

title: Number Pyramid
description:
Read `n` and print a centered pyramid of numbers. Row `i` (starting at 1) has `n - i` leading spaces followed by the digits `1` to `i` and then back down to `1`, with no separators. For n = 3:
`  1`
` 121`
`12321`

Input
One integer n.

Output
n lines forming the pyramid.
hint: For each row, print leading spaces, count upward from 1, then count back down to 1.
solutionNotes: Each row starts with its padding, then prints an ascending sequence and a descending sequence without repeating the peak.

title: Minimum Coins for Change
description:
You have unlimited coins of value 25, 10, 5 and 1. Given an amount, print how many coins of each kind the greedy method uses (largest coin first), and the total number of coins.

Input
One integer amount.

Output
Four lines: `25: a`, `10: b`, `5: c`, `1: d`, then a fifth line `Total: t`.
hint: Process coin values from largest to smallest. For each value, use division for its count and remainder for what is left.
solutionNotes: For each denomination, division gives how many coins fit. Keep the remainder for the next denomination and accumulate the total.
